method: Edited actual Beacon screenshots from isolated local runtime. Fictional intake and deterministic review fixtures; no real call or model inference.

scenes.title: Help starts with a report.
scenes.label: PHAROS / BEACON
scenes.caption: Fictional data • isolated local workspace • edited screen captures

scenes.title: See who needs attention.
scenes.label: 01 / URGENCY QUEUE
scenes.body: Reported needs set the suggested order. Service-area filters help responders focus.
scenes.caption: Every report keeps its urgency rank. Humans confirm the response.

scenes.title: Turn words into a case.
scenes.label: 02 / FICTIONAL INTAKE
scenes.body: Process a sample transcript through the backend. Three people. A specific landmark. A shelter need.
scenes.caption: This is sample text processing, not a phone call or speech-recognition result.

scenes.title: Keep the facts visible.
scenes.label: 03 / STRUCTURED REQUEST
scenes.body: Beacon preserves the caller’s words and location, then explains suggested urgency and coverage.
scenes.caption: No supported concern does not verify identity or establish that a report is true.

scenes.title: Start with the current need.
scenes.label: 04 / EVOLVING CASE
scenes.body: A fictional caller reports three people safely waiting for shelter near Riverbend footbridge.
scenes.caption: From here, call events and review results are controlled local fixtures. No phone or model service is invoked.

scenes.title: Let new danger change priority.
scenes.label: 05 / WORSENING CALLBACK
scenes.body: The same fictional situation now includes rising indoor water and no safe exit. The continuing case is reassessed.
scenes.caption: Fresh consent + explicit same-situation intent + matching location allow conservative linkage.

scenes.title: Preserve how the situation changed.
scenes.label: 06 / CASE HISTORY
scenes.body: Two linked reports remain available. The latest facts guide the current response without erasing the earlier report.
scenes.caption: Unknown or ambiguous matches stay separate. Caller ID is not proof of identity.

scenes.title: Hold response for human review.
scenes.label: 07 / EVIDENCE AND REVIEW
scenes.body: A fictional unsafe request has exact quoted evidence. Normal assignment and ETA are held; verification ownership remains possible.
scenes.caption: Content concerns do not lower urgency or erase reported danger. This review result is a fixed fixture.

scenes.title: Make the decision accountable.
scenes.label: 08 / REASONED ACCEPTANCE
scenes.body: The reviewer records a reason against the current evidence before accepting the report for response.
scenes.caption: This is a fictional reviewer action. Acceptance authorizes response work; it does not certify truth.

scenes.title: Acceptance opens the next step.
scenes.label: 09 / ELIGIBLE RESPONSE
scenes.body: The decision is recorded with its evidence scope. Coverage and responder eligibility still require confirmation.
scenes.caption: New concerns can require review again. Old reassurance does not automatically return.

scenes.title: Claiming establishes ownership.
scenes.label: 10 / RESPONDER ASSIGNMENT
scenes.body: An approved fictional team claims the accepted case. A claim alone does not confirm travel or arrival.
scenes.caption: Eligibility checks include area, capability, availability, approval, and capacity.

scenes.title: Report an estimate explicitly.
scenes.label: 11 / DESK-REPORTED PROGRESS
scenes.body: Choose On the way and enter a fresh ten-minute estimate. The desk owns the status update.
scenes.caption: On the way and Delayed require a current estimate of 1–180 minutes.

scenes.title: Be precise about reassurance.
scenes.label: 12 / CURRENT STATUS
scenes.body: Beacon shows who reported the update and when. Arrival remains an estimate; time passing never confirms arrival.
scenes.caption: During an active real intake, only a current server-authored desk update can be spoken. No audio is demonstrated here.

scenes.title: Human decisions. Clear evidence.
scenes.label: PHAROS / PRODUCT LIBRARY
scenes.body: Explore the manual, test cases, and system design on the product website.
scenes.caption: HackUTD prototype • fictional walkthrough • no real dispatch or phone/model acceptance claimed
